ports.note: A source. The output is a keyed table with no geometry and no CRS, which is why it is not the points port: flattening a table to points would mint one point per row and lose the key.

ontology.note:
GAP, meaning no alignment to an external tabular vocabulary -- not meaning the terms are undeclared. fw:DataTable and fw:TabularInput are declared in ontology/runtime.ttl with their properties, so the coupling gate passes on every term the receipt asserts.

WHY `emits` IS EMPTY WHILE THIS WIDGET'S RECEIPT ASSERTS NINETEEN TERMS. The field is measured against the release's `definition`, which for an input widget is src/core.ts#TYPES and asserts nothing of its own; the receipt is built in src/data-table.ts, which is listed under implementation.files and is not the definition. So the drift signal `emits` exists to give -- a change to the terms forcing a release -- does not cover this widget, and the terms are named here instead: DataTable and TabularInput, with boundAttribute, distinctValue, distinctValueCount, distinctValuesOf, keyField, measureKeyField, meltedValueField, meltedValueFieldCount, readAs, sourceDigest, sourceFile, subjectKeyField, tableMissingValueCount, tableRowCount, valueField, valueUnit and valueUnitStatus. Recorded as a limitation rather than worked around by moving the definition, which would be a claim about where this widget is implemented in order to satisfy a checker.

WHAT 0.2.0 ADDS is the shape of the READING rather than of the table: fw:readAs is asserted on the activity for both shapes, because a file that was already long is as much a fact about the reading as a melt is, and for a melt the subject keys, the measure key and each column taken are named. They hang off the activity and not off the table on purpose -- the table is long either way and only the reading differs. The melted columns are NAMED rather than inferred from what is left over, so a column absent from a receipt was not asked for rather than not present, and that distinction is the one a reader of a published figure needs.

changes.description: A value can be edited by hand in Data quality, under Records (experiment 214): kept on the step as an edit with the value it replaced and when, applied to a copy of the records when they are handed on, never to the file; an empty value can be filled, and such edits are counted apart (the practitioner, 2026-11-13: "Yes, like any edit"). An edit whose value read is no longer there is not applied, and is reported. Edits (n) lists them, each removable. The run states each as fw:CellEdit. The practitioner, 2026-11-10: "the ability to edit tables inline".

evidence.note: Unit checks cover the long-format contract, duplicate key rejection, missing values retained and counted, stated and unstated units, absent columns and the row cap.
